hypothesis: Every cold open boots a fresh worker and every spawned child is a fresh process, so #2857's process-global runtime-ready memo never fires there: the full probe chain (content walk + RUNTIME_READY_CHECK + dill import) is paid per fresh process.
approach: A cross-process on-disk memo <venv>/.runtime-probe-memo.json (bounded 16-key map, clear-at-cap, schema field) keyed by the SAME identity composite as #2857's in-process memo; lookup order in-process -> disk -> real probes; the key is recomputed fresh on every check (the content walk stays on the hit path as the damage detector - only the two interpreter probes are skipped); atomic per-pid temp+rename writes inside the venv dir (rename replaces a symlink, never follows); fail-open on every I/O error; invalidate_runtime_probe_cache() (unchanged signature, call sites byte-identical) clears both layers, with delete -> atomic empty-map-overwrite fallback when the delete fails; custom PRIME_AGENT_KERNEL_PYTHON override untouched (d14 ruling; behavioral pin: no memo file created under the override path).
parity_notes: Design pre-passes: BOTH adversarial reviewers approved at design level with binding conditions, all implemented + pinned by tests: (R2-A/R1-d) guaranteed-effective disk invalidation with the empty-map fallback + undeletable-file test + read-only-venv equivalence; (R2-B) the widened blind-spot window disclosed as an amendment - in #2857 the in-process memo died with the process (self-heal at next process start); the disk memo persists across processes so the masking window widens from process-lifetime to until-first-failed-start, same single-failure-then-heal end state (any kernel-start failure fires the invalidation, both layers drop, pinned by the masked-class-on-disk test); (R2-C/R1-e) cross-process oracles: hit-with-ZERO-interpreter-invocations after in-process-only clear, damage-across-processes matrix; (R2-D/R1-a) write-vs-invalidate race benign + tested, NO locking (cost equals base's own behavior); (R1-5/R2) stale/forged/symlink/directory/corrupt matrix; (R1-c) trust-domain sentence: the memo file's trust equals the venv's own (anyone who can write the venv can already inject kernel Python) - no new attack surface; (R1-e) the extended live witness (restore dill -> re-probe -> fresh-process disk hit with ZERO real interpreter invocations); LIVE-GATED closure-freeze test (operator-adopted): AST-parses the INSTALLED rlm sources with the real python and asserts the probe import closure's module-level imports are stdlib-or-rlm-relative (transitive walk; on first live run it found 18 real stdlib imports missing from the allowlist while the closure property itself held - zero third-party imports; allowlist completed, both live tests 2/2 PASS at the final head). The dill-heal-before-start behavior is inherited from #2857: the CURRENT base also repairs (the pre-#2857 base-fails-at-snapshot delta is HISTORICAL - both sides of this pair repair heal-before-start, verified at the final head).
